lots.key_photo_findings: One photo (442687_1.jpg) viewed at full size. Chalk '1107 9/10/26' and a round lot sticker. Freshly band-sawn faces, live edges with fibrous bark remnants, a deep V fork at the top with a bark-lined crack running into the crotch. Pale cream sapwood with heavy darker streaks. The figure is consistent with the pale outer wood of Moreton Bay chestnut (Castanospermum australe), whose heartwood is darker chocolate-brown, but it could also be camphor laurel or another streaky hardwood. The researcher's olive suggestion is unlikely for a slab this size. Looks recently milled and probably unseasoned.
lots.condition: Raw, rough-sawn, likely green. Crack running down from the fork crotch; bark inclusion. No obvious end checks visible but ends not photographed closely. Will need drying and flattening before use.
lots.question_for_gowans: What are the length, width and thickness of the slab, and when was it milled (is it green or air dried)? How is the species known to be Moreton Bay chestnut? Does the crack at the fork run right through the slab? Will staff help load it at Moonah?
